Cricket final

The **2025 Indian Premier League final** was a [Twenty20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twenty20 "Twenty20") (T20) [cricket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cricket "Cricket") match played at the [Narendra Modi Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narendra_Modi_Stadium "Narendra Modi Stadium") in [Ahmedabad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad "Ahmedabad"), India, on 3 June 2025 to determine the winner of the [2025 Indian Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Indian_Premier_League "2025 Indian Premier League") (IPL). It was originally scheduled to be played at [Eden Gardens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eden_Gardens "Eden Gardens") in [Kolkata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata "Kolkata"), on 25 May 2025 before being [rescheduled](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Indian_Premier_League#Suspension_and_rescheduling "2025 Indian Premier League").

It was played between [Royal Challengers Bengaluru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Challengers_Bengaluru "Royal Challengers Bengaluru") and [Punjab Kings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punjab_Kings "Punjab Kings"). Punjab won the toss and elected to field first; Bengaluru scored 190/9 in their innings. In the second innings, Punjab scored 184/7. Bengaluru won the match by 6 runs to win their maiden IPL trophy after 18 years.

## Background

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=2025_Indian_Premier_League_final&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background")]

Main article: [2025 Indian Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Indian_Premier_League "2025 Indian Premier League")

The [2025 Indian Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Indian_Premier_League "2025 Indian Premier League") was the 18th edition of the [Indian Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Premier_League "Indian Premier League") (IPL), a professional [Twenty20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twenty20 "Twenty20") (T20) [cricket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cricket "Cricket") league, organised by the [Board of Control for Cricket in India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Board_of_Control_for_Cricket_in_India "Board of Control for Cricket in India") (BCCI).[[1]](#cite_note-1) On 16 February, the fixtures for the season were confirmed with the 2025 season set to commence from 22 March with 10 teams competing in 74 matches across 13 venues.[[2]](#cite_note-2) The final was scheduled for 25 May at [Eden Gardens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eden_Gardens "Eden Gardens"), [Kolkata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata "Kolkata") with the venue to host its third IPL final after [2013](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Indian_Premier_League_final "2013 Indian Premier League final") and [2015](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Indian_Premier_League_final "2015 Indian Premier League final").[[3]](#cite_note-3)

On 9 May 2025, the remaining matches were suspended due to the [2025 India–Pakistan crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_India–Pakistan_crisis "2025 India–Pakistan crisis").[[4]](#cite_note-4) The revised schedule was announced on 12 May, and the remaining matches resumed on 17 May and were held across six venues.[[5]](#cite_note-res1-5)[[6]](#cite_note-res2-6) On 20 May, the playoff fixtures were confirmed[[7]](#cite_note-res-po-7) with the final rescheduled for 3 June at the [Narendra Modi Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narendra_Modi_Stadium "Narendra Modi Stadium"), [Ahmedabad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad "Ahmedabad") with the venue hosting its third final after [2022](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Indian_Premier_League_final "2022 Indian Premier League final") and [2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Indian_Premier_League_final "2023 Indian Premier League final").[[8]](#cite_note-8)

[Royal Challengers Bengaluru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Challengers_Bengaluru "Royal Challengers Bengaluru") qualified for their fourth IPL final after being runners-up in [2009](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_Indian_Premier_League_final "2009 Indian Premier League final"), [2011](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Indian_Premier_League_final "2011 Indian Premier League final") and [2016](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League_final "2016 Indian Premier League final"),[[9]](#cite_note-9) while [Punjab Kings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punjab_Kings "Punjab Kings") qualified for their second IPL final after being runners-up in [2014](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League_final "2014 Indian Premier League final").[[10]](#cite_note-10) Both teams were competing for their maiden titles.[[11]](#cite_note-hist-11)

The **2025 Indian Premier League**, also known as **IPL 18** and branded as **TATA IPL 2025**, was the 18th edition of the [Indian Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Premier_League "Indian Premier League"), a professional [Twenty20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twenty20 "Twenty20") [cricket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cricket "Cricket") league. The tournament featured 10 teams competing in 74 matches. It began on 22 March and was held across 13 venues before being suspended on 9 May due to the [2025 India–Pakistan crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_India–Pakistan_crisis "2025 India–Pakistan crisis"). The matches resumed from 17 May across six venues, with the [final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Indian_Premier_League_final "2025 Indian Premier League final") rescheduled from 25 May to 3 June.

The defending champions [Kolkata Knight Riders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_Knight_Riders "Kolkata Knight Riders") were eliminated in the league stage. In the [final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Indian_Premier_League_final "2025 Indian Premier League final"), [Royal Challengers Bengaluru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Challengers_Bengaluru "Royal Challengers Bengaluru") defeated [Punjab Kings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punjab_Kings "Punjab Kings") by 6 runs to win their maiden title after 18 years. [Sai Sudharsan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sai_Sudharsan "Sai Sudharsan") and [Prasidh Krishna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prasidh_Krishna "Prasidh Krishna") of [Gujarat Titans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gujarat_Titans "Gujarat Titans") scored the most runs (759) and took the most wickets (25). [Suryakumar Yadav](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suryakumar_Yadav "Suryakumar Yadav") of [Mumbai Indians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumbai_Indians "Mumbai Indians") was named as the most valuable player of the tournament.

Royal Challengers Bengaluru successfully defended their IPL title by beating the Gujarat Titans in the IPL 2026 final at Narendra Modi Stadium in Ahmedabad.
